title: Hong Kong DAB chairman estimates 17 organisations hacked in two months, 3.12 million people's data leaked; party seeks contractor rules
date_note: Sing Tao's page, dated 27 November, gives no earlier day for the statements.
org: Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong (DAB)
summary: According to Sing Tao, DAB chairman Chan Hak-kan gave a preliminary estimate that 17 organisations, including companies, universities and medical institutions, were hacked within two months, with personal data of 3.12 million people leaked. DAB vice-chairman Chow Ho-ding said Hong Kong has no law regulating outsourced contractors of organisations holding personal data, and called for a breach-notification mechanism.
plain: A Hong Kong party leader estimates 17 organisations were hacked in two months, with data of 3.12 million people leaked, and wants contractors regulated. It is his preliminary estimate.
exec: A DAB leader's preliminary estimate cites 3.12 million people affected and calls for rules on outsourced contractors.
geo_basis: country: Hong Kong, where the DAB made the statements
